prompts.prompt:
STORY BRIEF
- Protagonist: A lone exorcist with forgotten powers
- Goal: Uncover the truth behind a shattered world
- Genre: Dark Fantasy
- World rule (must matter to the plot): Magic exists, but every spell costs the caster a memory
- Ending twist (reveal near the climax, set it up earlier): The real villain is the protagonist's future self
- Tone: dark and grim (30/100 toward light)
- Conflict level: high (80/100)
- Romance: none or minimal (30/100)
- Action intensity: intense battles (85/100)
- Length: 4 chapters of about 330 words each

Write the story. Return JSON with this schema:
{
  "title": string,
  "logline": string (2-3 sentence teaser),
  "characters": [{"name": string, "role": "protagonist"|"ally"|"rival"|"villain"|"mentor"|"other",
                  "visual_description": string (hair, eyes, outfit; reused for every image)}]  (3-5 items),
  "relationships": [{"source": name, "target": name, "label": short string like "ALLY", "CONFLICT"}],
  "beats": [{"name": one of "Inciting Incident","Call to Action","Rising Conflict","Midpoint Turn","Climax","Resolution",
             "summary": one sentence}]  (exactly 6, in that order),
  "chapters": [{"title": short title WITHOUT "Chapter" or a number, "text": string}],
  "scenes": [{"caption": short string, "image_prompt": visual description of one key moment, no dialogue}]  (exactly 4)
}

output.title: The Memory Eater
output.logline: A lone exorcist casts forbidden spells to mend a shattered world, unaware that every forgotten memory brings him closer to becoming the very monster he hunts. In a realm consumed by darkness, the ultimate enemy wears his own face.

chapters.title: Ash and Echoes
chapters.text:
The wind howled across the desolate plains of Oakhaven, carrying the scent of sulfur and old blood. Kaelen knelt beside a twitching corpse of a shadow fiend, his breath pluming in the freezing air. He could not remember why he carried the heavy iron blade at his side, nor could he picture the face of his mother. Every spell required a toll, and Kaelen had paid in the currency of his own mind.

"Another village gone," Lyra whispered, stepping over the shattered remnants of a wooden barricade. Her emerald eyes scanned the horizon where the sky bled an unnatural bruised purple. "The rifts are expanding, Kaelen. If we don't reach the core, the entire world will unravel."

Kaelen stood up, his amber eyes blank yet fiercely focused. He raised his hand, tracing a glowing rune in the air to seal a minor spatial tear. As the energy flared, a sharp pain pierced his temples. The memory of his first sword stroke vanished entirely, replaced by a hollow void. He gritted his teeth against the mental bleed.

"I know," Kaelen muttered, his voice raspy. "And every time I fight them, I leave a piece of myself behind. Lead the way, Lyra. Let's finish this before I forget why I started."

chapters.title: Path of Thorns
chapters.text:
The journey toward the World Core was fraught with danger. Corrupted beasts lunged from the gloom, their forms shifting like smoke and jagged glass. Lyra fought with precision, her dual daggers flashing in the dim light, but the heavier burdens fell upon Kaelen.

When a horde of wraiths surrounded them, Kaelen had no choice. He slammed his palms into the scorched earth, chanting an ancient exorcism incantation. A blinding dome of golden light erupted, incinerating the spirits instantly. But the cost was catastrophic.

Kaelen stumbled, dropping to one knee as blood trickled from his nose. His mind reeled. His best friend's name, the face of the woman he had loved, the very reason he became an exorcist—all of it dissolved into mist. He looked up at Lyra with wide, terrified eyes, completely unable to recognize her face.

"Kaelen?" Lyra asked, rushing to his side, her voice laced with panic. "What did you lose this time?"

"Who... are you?" Kaelen whispered, gripping his head as the agonizing silence of his empty memories threatened to crush his sanity.

"I'm Lyra," she said, her voice trembling. "We've been fighting together for months. Please, hold on to me."

Kaelen clenched his fists, using sheer willpower to steady himself. He didn't know her, but the burning drive within his chest remained. He had to reach the core.

chapters.title: The Fractured Truth
chapters.text:
They reached the precipice of the World Core, a massive chasm where reality fractured into floating shards of land suspended over an endless abyss. Waiting for them at the center of the platform was the Hollow King, shrouded in darkness and wielding a blade made of pure crystallized memories.

"You finally made it, past-self," a voice echoed from beneath the porcelain mask, chilling and deeply familiar. 

Kaelen drew his iron sword, his chest heaving. "Who are you? Show your face!"

Lyra backed away, her breath catching in her throat as the ominous aura of the king washed over them. "Kaelen, be careful. That entity... it radiates your exact magical signature."

Without warning, the Hollow King charged. The clash of steel shook the floating platform. Sparks flew into the dark abyss below as Kaelen parried blow after devastating blow. The king fought with ruthless efficiency, anticipating every move Kaelen made before he even executed it. It was like fighting a mirror image.

Driven by desperation, Kaelen invoked a forbidden spell, pouring his remaining essence into his blade. The sword blazed with blinding white fire, cutting through the king's defenses and slashing straight across the porcelain mask.

chapters.title: The Final Reflection
chapters.text:
The mask split in half and clattered to the stone floor. Kaelen froze, the glowing sword hovering inches from his opponent's throat. The face staring back at him was scarred, older, and undeniably his own.

"Now you see," the future Kaelen whispered, blood pooling at the corner of his mouth. "Every memory you sacrifice doesn't just disappear. It accumulates here. I am what remains after a lifetime of saving a world that cannot be saved. To stop the cycle, you must kill me—and take my place as the guardian of the void."

Kaelen looked back at Lyra, who stood paralyzed in horror. He realized the grim truth of his existence. There was no victory, only an endless loop of self-sacrifice and forgotten sorrow.

Lowering his sword, Kaelen embraced his future self. The magic flared one last time, consuming the last vestiges of his identity in a brilliant flash of white light. When the light faded, a lone figure in a charcoal coat stood silently at the edge of the chasm, wearing a fractured porcelain mask, waiting for the next traveler to arrive.
